blocks.p: When the town of Mansoul had rid itself thus far of its enemies and of the troublers of its peace, a strict order was given next that my Lord Willbewill, with Diligence his man, should hunt down and arrest whatever homegrown Diabolonians were still left alive in Mansoul. The names of several of them were Mr. Fooling, Mr. Let-Good-Slip, Mr. Slavish-Fear, Mr. No-Love, Mr. Mistrust, Mr. Flesh, and Mr. Sloth. He was also commanded to arrest the children Mr. Evil-Questioning had left behind him, and to demolish his house. The children he left behind were these: Mr. Doubt, his eldest son; and after him, Live-by-the-Law, Unbelief, Wrong-Thoughts-of-Christ, Clip-promise, Carnal-Sense, Live-by-Feeling, and Self-Love. All these he had by one wife, whose name was No-Hope. She was a kinswoman of old Incredulity, for he was her uncle; and when her father, old Dark, died, Incredulity took her and brought her up, and when she was of an age to marry, he gave her to old Evil-Questioning for his wife.

Now the Lord Willbewill carried out his commission with great diligence, and with Diligence his man. He caught Fooling in the streets and hanged him in Want-wit Alley (a want-wit being a fool), directly across from his own house. This Fooling was the one who would have had the town of Mansoul hand Captain Credence over to Diabolus, provided Diabolus would then withdraw his forces from the town. He also caught Mr. Let-Good-Slip one day as he was busy in the market, and executed him according to law. Now there was an honest poor man in Mansoul named Mr. Meditation, of no great account in the days when the town had fallen away, but now well thought of by the best people in it; so they were willing to advance him. Mr. Let-Good-Slip had once been very wealthy, and at Emmanuel’s coming his wealth had been confiscated for the Prince’s use. It was now given to Mr. Meditation, to put to work for the common good, and after him to his son, Mr. Think-Well. This Think-Well he had by Mrs. Piety his wife, who was the daughter of the Recorder.

After this my lord arrested Clip-promise. Now because he was a notorious villain (for by his doings much of the King’s coin had been abused: clipped, that is, shaved thin at the edges by a thief who keeps the shavings), he was made a public example. He was sentenced first to be set in the pillory, then to be whipped by all the children and servants in Mansoul, and then to be hanged until he was dead. Some may wonder at the severity of his punishment; but the honest traders of Mansoul know what great harm one clipper of promises can do to the town in a short time. And truly my judgment is that all of his name and way of life should be served just as he was.

He also arrested Carnal-Sense and locked him up; but how I cannot tell, he broke prison and escaped. Yes, and the bold villain will not leave the town even yet, but lurks in the Diabolonian dens by day and haunts honest men’s houses like a ghost by night. So a proclamation was posted in the marketplace, announcing that whoever could find Carnal-Sense, arrest him, and slay him should be admitted daily to the Prince’s table and made keeper of the treasure of Mansoul. Many set themselves to do it; but though he was often found, take him and slay him they could not.
But my lord took Mr. Wrong-Thoughts-of-Christ and put him in prison, and he died there; though it was a long while first, for he died of a slow, wasting consumption.

Self-Love was also taken into custody; but he had many relations in Mansoul, so his judgment was put off. But at last Mr. Self-Denial stood up and said, “If villains like this may be winked at in Mansoul, I will lay down my commission.” Then he took him out of the crowd and brought him among his soldiers, and there his brains were dashed out. Some in Mansoul muttered at it, though none dared speak plainly, with Emmanuel in town. But this brave act of Captain Self-Denial came to the Prince’s ears; so he sent for him and made him a lord in Mansoul. My Lord Willbewill also received great praise from Emmanuel for what he had done for the town of Mansoul.

Then my Lord Self-Denial took courage and set about pursuing the Diabolonians together with my Lord Willbewill; and they took Live-by-Feeling, and they took Live-by-the-Law, and kept them locked up until they died. But Mr. Unbelief was a nimble fellow; they could never lay hold of him, though they tried often. So he, and a few more of the subtlest of the Diabolonian tribe, remained in Mansoul until the day Mansoul ceased to dwell in the kingdom of Universe. But they kept them to their dens and holes. If one of them showed himself in any street of Mansoul, the whole town would be up in arms after him; yes, the very children of Mansoul would cry out after him as after a thief, and wish they might stone him to death. And now Mansoul came to a good measure of peace and quiet. Her Prince also stayed within her borders; her captains and her soldiers did their duty; and Mansoul attended to the trade she had with the country that was far away, and was busy in her own manufacture as well.

When the town of Mansoul had rid itself thus far of so many of its enemies and the troublers of its peace, the Prince appointed a day to meet the whole people in the marketplace and give them his charge concerning some further matters, which, if they kept them, would tend to their further safety and comfort, and to the condemnation and destruction of their homegrown Diabolonians. So the appointed day came, and the townspeople gathered together. Emmanuel also came down in his chariot, with all his captains in their state attending him on the right hand and on the left. Then a crier called “Oyez!” for silence, and after some tender exchanges of love on both sides, the Prince began, and spoke as follows.

“You, my Mansoul, and the beloved of my heart: many and great are the privileges I have given you. I have singled you out from others and chosen you for myself, not because you were worthy, but for my own sake. I have also redeemed you, not only from the terror of my Father’s law, but from the hand of Diabolus. This I have done because I loved you, and because I set my heart on you to do you good. I have also, so that everything that might hinder your way to the pleasures of paradise could be taken out of the way, paid for your soul the full satisfaction that justice demanded, and have bought you for myself: not at the price of corruptible things, such as silver and gold [1 Pet. 1:18], but at a price of blood, my own blood, which I freely poured out on the ground to make you mine. So I have reconciled you, O my Mansoul, to my Father, and have secured for you a place in the mansions that are with my Father in the royal city, where there are things, O my Mansoul, that eye has not seen, nor has it entered into the heart of man to conceive. [1 Cor. 2:9]

“Besides, O my Mansoul, you see what I have done, and how I have taken you out of the hands of your enemies, to whom you had gone over in deep revolt against my Father, and by whom you were content to be possessed, and destroyed as well. I came to you first by my law, then by my gospel, to awaken you and to show you my glory. And you know what you were, what you said, what you did, and how many times you rebelled against my Father and me; yet I did not leave you, as you see this day, but came to you, bore with your ways, waited on you, and after all accepted you, out of my mere grace and favor; and I would not let you be lost, as you would most willingly have been. I also surrounded you and afflicted you on every side, so that I might make you weary of your ways, and bring your heart down by trouble until you were willing to take hold of your own good and happiness. And when I had won a complete conquest over you, I turned it to your advantage.

“You see, too, what a company of my Father’s host I have lodged within your borders: captains and rulers, soldiers and men of war, engines and excellent devices to subdue and bring down your foes. You know what I mean, O Mansoul. And they are my servants, and yours too, Mansoul. Yes, my purpose in possessing you with them, and the natural tendency of each of them, is to defend, purge, strengthen, and sweeten you for myself, O Mansoul, and to make you fit for my Father’s presence, blessing, and glory; for you, my Mansoul, were created to be prepared for these.

“You see, moreover, my Mansoul, how I have passed over your backslidings and have healed you. Indeed I was angry with you, but I have turned my anger away from you, because I loved you still; and my anger and my indignation have come to an end in the destruction of your enemies, O Mansoul. Nor was it your goodness that brought me back to you after I had hidden my face and withdrawn my presence from you because of your transgressions. The way of backsliding was yours, but the way and means of your recovery were mine. I devised the means of your return. It was I who made a hedge and a wall when you were beginning to turn to things in which I took no delight. It was I who made your sweet bitter, your day night, your smooth way thorny, and who also confounded all who sought your destruction. It was I who set Mr. Godly-Fear to work in Mansoul. It was I who stirred up your conscience and your understanding, your will and your affections, after your great and woeful decay. It was I who put life into you, O Mansoul, to seek me, so that you might find me, and in finding me find your own health, happiness, and salvation. It was I who drove the Diabolonians out of Mansoul the second time; and it was I who overcame them and destroyed them before your face.

“And now, my Mansoul, I have returned to you in peace, and your transgressions against me are as if they had never been. Nor shall it be with you as in former days; I will do better for you than at your beginning. [Ezek. 36:11]

“For yet a little while, O my Mansoul, even after a few more seasons have passed over your head, I will (but do not be troubled at what I say) take down this famous town of Mansoul, stick and stone, to the ground. And I will carry its stones, and its timber, and its walls, and its dust, and its inhabitants, into my own country, into a kingdom of my Father; and there I will set it up in such strength and glory as it never saw in the kingdom where it now stands. I will set it up there for my Father’s dwelling place; for that was the purpose for which it was first built in the kingdom of Universe. And there I will make it a spectacle of wonder, a monument of mercy, and a marveler at its own mercy. There the natives of Mansoul shall see all that of which they have seen nothing here; there they shall be equal to those to whom they have been inferior here. And there, O my Mansoul, you shall have such fellowship with me, with my Father, and with your Lord Secretary as it is not possible to enjoy here, nor ever could be, though you should live in Universe for a thousand years.

“And there, O my Mansoul, you shall be afraid of murderers no more; of Diabolonians and their threats, no more. There, there shall be no more plots, or schemes, or designs against you, O my Mansoul. There you shall no more hear evil tidings, or the noise of the Diabolonian drum. There you shall not see the Diabolonian standard-bearers, nor behold Diabolus’s standard. No Diabolonian siege mound shall be thrown up against you there, nor shall the Diabolonian standard be set up there to make you afraid. There you shall not need captains, engines, soldiers, and men of war. There you shall meet with no sorrow or grief; nor shall it be possible for any Diabolonian ever again to creep into your skirts, burrow in your walls, or be seen again within your borders, all the days of eternity. Life there shall last longer than you are able here to desire it should; and yet it shall always be sweet and new, and nothing shall ever stand in its way, forever.

“There, O Mansoul, you shall meet many who have been like you, and who have shared your sorrows: such as I have chosen, and redeemed, and set apart, as I did you, for my Father’s court and royal city. They will all be glad of you; and you, when you see them, shall be glad in your heart.

“There are things, O Mansoul, things of my Father’s providing and mine, that have never been seen since the beginning of the world; and they are laid up with my Father, and sealed up among his treasures for you, until you come there to enjoy them. I told you before that I would remove my Mansoul and set it up somewhere else; and where I will set it, there are those who love you, and those who rejoice in you now. But how much more will they rejoice when they see you exalted to honor! My Father will then send them to fetch you; and their bosoms are chariots to carry you in. And you, O my Mansoul, shall ride on the wings of the wind. They will come to convey you, conduct you, and bring you to that place which, when your eyes see more, will be your desired haven.

“And so, O my Mansoul, I have shown you what shall be done for you hereafter, if you can hear, if you can understand. And now I will tell you what your duty and practice must be for the present, until I come and fetch you to myself, as it is recorded in the Scriptures of truth.

“First, I charge you that from now on you keep whiter and cleaner the liveries, the garments of my household, which I gave you before my last withdrawing from you. Do it, I say, for this will be your wisdom. In themselves they are fine linen, but you must keep them white and clean. This will be your wisdom and your honor, and will be greatly for my glory. When your garments are white, the world will count you mine. Also, when your garments are white, then I delight in your ways; for then your goings to and fro will be like a flash of lightning, which those who are present must take notice of; their very eyes will be dazzled by it. Adorn yourself, therefore, as I bid you, and by my law make straight steps for your feet; so shall your King greatly desire your beauty, for he is your Lord, and worship him. [Ps. 45:11]

“Now, so that you may keep them as I bid you, I have, as I told you before, provided an open fountain for you to wash your garments in. See to it, then, that you wash often in my fountain, and do not go about in defiled garments; for as that is to my dishonor and my disgrace, so it will be to your own discomfort, when you walk in filthy garments. Do not let my garments, then, your garments, the garments I gave you, be defiled or spotted by the flesh. Keep your garments always white, and let your head lack no ointment. [Eccl. 9:8]

“My Mansoul, I have many times delivered you from the designs, plots, attempts, and conspiracies of Diabolus; and for all this I ask nothing of you, except that you do not repay me evil for my good, but that you keep in mind my love, and the continuance of my kindness to my beloved Mansoul, so that it moves you to walk, in your measure, in keeping with the benefit given you. Of old, the sacrifices were bound with cords to the horns of the altar. [Ps. 118:27] Consider what is said to you, O my blessed Mansoul.

“O my Mansoul, I have lived, I have died, I live, and I will die no more for you. I live so that you may not die. Because I live, you shall live also. [John 14:19] I reconciled you to my Father by the blood of my cross; and being reconciled, you shall live through me. I will pray for you; I will fight for you; I will yet do you good.
“Nothing can hurt you but sin; nothing can grieve me but sin; nothing can make you contemptible before your foes but sin. Beware of sin, my Mansoul.

“And do you know why I allowed at first, and still allow, Diabolonians to dwell within your walls, O Mansoul? It is to keep you awake, to test your love, to make you watchful, and to make you still prize my noble captains, their soldiers, and my mercy.

“It is also so that you may be made to remember what a deplorable condition you were once in. I mean when not some, but all of them dwelt, not in your walls, but in your castle and in your stronghold, O Mansoul.

“O my Mansoul, if I should slay all those within, there are many without who would bring you into bondage; for if all those within were cut off, those without would find you sleeping, and then, as in a moment, they would swallow up my Mansoul. Therefore I left them in you, not to do you harm (which they still will, if you listen to them and serve them), but to do you good, which they must, if you watch and fight against them. Know, therefore, that whatever they tempt you to, my design is that they should drive you not further off, but nearer to my Father: to teach you war, to make petitioning desirable to you, and to make you little in your own eyes. Listen carefully to this, my Mansoul.

“Show me your love, then, my Mansoul, and do not let those who are within your walls draw your affections away from him who has redeemed your soul. Yes, let the very sight of a Diabolonian heighten your love for me. I came once, and twice, and three times, to save you from the poison of those arrows that would have worked your death. Stand for me, your Friend, my Mansoul, against the Diabolonians, and I will stand for you before my Father and all his court. Love me against temptation, and I will love you in spite of your weaknesses.

“O my Mansoul, remember what my captains, my soldiers, and my engines have done for you. They have fought for you, they have suffered at your hands, they have borne much from you in order to do you good, O Mansoul. If you had not had them to help you, Diabolus would certainly have made an end of you. Nourish them, therefore, my Mansoul. When you do well, they will be well; when you do ill, they will be ill, and sick, and weak. Do not make my captains sick, O Mansoul; for if they are sick, you cannot be well; if they are weak, you cannot be strong; if they are faint, you cannot be stout and valiant for your King, O Mansoul. Nor must you think to live always by what you can see and feel; you must live on my word. You must believe, O my Mansoul, when I am away from you, that I love you still, and carry you on my heart forever.

“Remember, therefore, O my Mansoul, that you are beloved by me. As I have taught you to watch, to fight, to pray, and to make war against my foes, so now I command you to believe that my love for you is constant. O my Mansoul, how I have set my heart, my love, upon you! Watch. Behold, I lay no other burden on you [Rev. 2:24] than what you have already. Hold fast till I come.” [Rev. 2:25]
